query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small amount of zirconium (~2 at.%) to MnNiSi-based alloys will improve their mechanical performance by refining the microstructure and enhancing ductility while largely retaining the strong magnetocaloric effect.
generation.material_initial_state: MnNiSi alloy exhibiting a large magnetocaloric effect but with limited mechanical toughness and ductility.
generation.intervention: Introduce a microalloying addition of approximately 2 at.% Zr into the MnNiSi alloy composition.
generation.conditions: Samples are prepared via conventional melting and casting followed by a controlled annealing process to ensure homogeneous distribution of Zr. Measurements are performed near the magnetocaloric transition temperature under standard operational conditions for refrigeration applications.
generation.structural_mediator: The addition of Zr is expected to promote grain refinement and modify grain boundaries via solid solution strengthening, which mitigates defect propagation.
generation.mechanism: The larger atomic radius of Zr atoms leads to local lattice distortions that refine the microstructure and enhance ductility. At the same time, because the concentration is kept low, the critical magnetic interactions within the MnNiSi matrix remain largely unperturbed, thereby retaining the large magnetic entropy change characteristic of the material.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Zr-alloyed MnNiSi will show improved mechanical properties (increased ductility and possibly higher yield strength) relative to the unalloyed baseline while maintaining a magnetocaloric effect (ΔSm and transition temperature) that is within about 15% of the original performance.
generation.baseline: Unalloyed MnNiSi alloy, which exhibits a large magnetocaloric effect but has brittle mechanical behavior.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is expected only for small Zr additions (around 2 at.%); higher levels might dilute the magnetic interactions, reducing the magnetocaloric performance.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal exact amount of Zr and its precise impact on both mechanical and magnetocaloric properties remain to be thoroughly mapped. The trade-off between improved ductility and possible minor shifts in the magnetic transition temperature is uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of MnNiSi-based alloy samples with 0, 1, 2, and 3 at.% Zr additions. All samples undergo identical melting, casting, and annealing processes to ensure homogeneity. Test mechanical properties (e.g., tensile yield strength and ductility) and magnetocaloric characteristics (e.g., magnetic entropy change ΔSm and transition temperature) under the same thermal and magnetic field cycling conditions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the sample with approximately 2 at.% Zr addition does not exhibit at least a 20% improvement in mechanical properties (e.g., ductility, strength) relative to the baseline MnNiSi alloy, or if its magnetocaloric effect (ΔSm) decreases by more than 15% relative to the baseline, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

Tunable magnetocaloric effect in transition metal alloys

Abstract: The unpredictability of geopolitical tensions and resulting supply chain and pricing instabilities make it imperative to explore rare earth free magnetic materials. As such, we have investigated fully transition metal based “high entropy alloys” in the context of the magnetocaloric effect. We find the NiFeCoCrPdx family exhibits a second order magnetic phase transition whose critical temperature is tunable from 100 K to well above room temperature. The system notably displays changes in the functionality of the magnetic entropy change depending on x, which leads to nearly 40% enhancement of the refrigerant capacity. A detailed statistical analysis of the universal scaling behavior provides direct evidence that heat treatment and Pd additions reduce the distribution of exchange energies in the system, leading to a more magnetically homogeneous alloy. The general implications of this work are that the parent NiFeCoCr compound can be tuned dramatically with FCC metal additives. Remarkable Enhanced Mechanical Properties of TiAlCrNbV Medium-Entropy Alloy with Zr Additions

Abstract: Most medium entropy alloys (MEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties, but their applications are limited because of their high density. This study explores a series of lightweight nonequiatomic Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx (x = 3, 5, 7, and 10) MEAs with a low density, high strength, and high ductility. To achieve solid solution strengthening, Zr with a large atomic radius was used. In addition, various thermomechanical treatment parameters were adopted to further improve the MEAs’ mechanical properties. The density of the MEAs was revealed to be approximately 5 g/cm3, indicating that they were lightweight. Through an X-ray diffraction analysis, the MEAs were revealed to have a single body-centered cubic structure not only in the as-cast state but also after thermomechanical treatment. In terms of mechanical properties, all the as-cast MEAs with Zr additions achieved excellent performance (>1000 MPa tensile yield strength and 20% tensile ductility).
